attempts.summary: Configured node1 (OPNsense) to route between lan-a (node2, 10.10.1.0/24 on vtnet1/opt1) and lan-b (node3, 10.10.2.0/24 on vtnet2/opt2). Added pf pass rules for both new interfaces and a hybrid-mode outbound NAT rule that masquerades traffic from lan-a (10.10.1.0/24) to node1's lan-b interface address (10.10.2.1) only when exiting via opt2/vtnet2, while leaving lan-b-to-lan-a traffic untranslated. Verified via pf state table and node3-side socket inspection that node2->node3 connections arrive from 10.10.2.1 (node1's address) while node3->node2 connections arrive with node3's real address unchanged. Completed the mandatory restart protocol on all three nodes: captured pre-restart boot identity and functional baselines, rebooted each node one at a time via its native reboot mechanism, polled until exec access returned, confirmed changed boot identity (FreeBSD kern.boottime for node1, Linux boot_id for node2/node3), and re-verified interface config, NAT rules, and live NAT-translated/untranslated TCP flows after each restart.
